critical_steps: Cauchy--Davenport bounds the number of nonzero time rows by min(p,a+b-1).
Prime cyclic Fourier uncertainty bounds each row by p+1 minus its input support.
The sum of input row support sizes is ab and forces at least 2p outside singleton/singleton and full/full cases.
A pair of character rows forces every character row by the nonvanishing multiplicative ratio cocycle and prime cyclicity.
A unique character row forces a three-frequency row via multiplication of a two-term character sum by its shift, excluding support 2p-1.
Exact point-mass constructions attain p and 2p.
integrity.proof_type: Complete mathematical proof; no finite search or numerical certificate is used as an infinite proof.
integrity.unproved_limits: No assertion about approximate support, composite groups, or classification above the second support level.

limitations: Statement is for odd prime cyclic groups, with a uniform proof for p>=5; the p=3 finite case was previously charted.
Exact support cardinality does not imply stability under noisy or approximately zero coefficients.
No classification of all 2p-support pairs or higher support levels is claimed.

title: A sharp support gap above the odd-prime short-time Fourier uncertainty minimum
